02
The framework

Playing Principles

Our principles drive every action in training and competition.

  • Tactical clarity: every player owns their role and priority in each situation.
  • Smart aggression: we attack and defend with intent, never losing control.
  • Setting tempo: we speed up execution while holding precision and court awareness.
  • System discipline: we respect the pre-set structure for clean execution.
  • Reading the game: we interpret the context to decide with an edge.
  • Role responsibility: discipline and consistency in every function.
  • Emotional stability: we train the way we play — always at 100%.

03
How we score

Offensive System

  • Rotation-based setting: we adjust the set to where the pass drops, shifting systems to create numerical advantage against the block.
  • Middle involvement: middles are a constant threat in side-out and transition, with varied tempos and trajectories.
  • Tempo variability: we adapt set height and speed to ball quality to manage our attack.
  • Aggressive transition: we convert the counter-attack through set quality and disciplined hitting.
  • The block as a tool: more than an end, it steers the rival attack into our strong defensive zones.
  • Setter leadership: offensive rhythm, smart shot selection and balanced distribution by rotation, read and context.
  • Hitter efficiency: variety of shots, tools and decisions — telling a tactical error from a technical one.
  • Hit hard, high and deep, varying angles and never closing the swing.
  • Be smart: recycle when needed and always target the last 3 meters of the court.

04
How we defend

Defensive System

  • The block as a tool: more than a direct kill, we guide the rival attack into the zone where our defenders wait.
  • System organization: we defend on pre-set patterns by rotation, rival tendencies and the opposing setter's distribution.
  • Collective reading: we trigger the system off the rival pass and move with the opposing set.
  • Dig-to-attack: after the dig we look for a fast, orderly transition into real counter-attack options.
  • Role responsibility: each player owns their defensive job with discipline, communication and technical precision.
  • Controlled aggression: we defend with intent, keeping body balance, controlled rebounds and rally continuity.
  • No ball hits the floor without our players first going after it.

05
Side-out + transition

Blocking System

Read  decision by rival trajectory and setter distribution.
Call 1  priority front half (middle · pipe · position 4).
Call 2  priority back half (middle · pipe · position 2/1).
Commit  we follow the middle; on a perfect ball we block 1-on-1.
Pin & pin  priority on the antennas.
  • We block the ball, not a zone.  ▶ VIDEO
  • The pin takes the ball; the middle closes mainly the cross-court.
  • The off-blocker drops fast to cover the sharp angle.
  • We watch: pass drop, set direction, ball path and the hitter's approach.
  • Ball quality changes the block — a double-positive isn't a high, separated ball. Good reading sets jump timing and contact.
  • THE DEFENSE CALLS OUT WHEN THERE IS NO BLOCK.

06
Concept & system

Serve

MINDSET

We are aggressive from this fundamental. The serve is our first real chance to win the point — executed with intent, pressure and reading of the rival.

MAIN OBJECTIVES

Jump serve → ace. Float → hurt or neutralize a specific passer per game plan. First serve of each set and post-timeout: must be in. Stay flexible to what the team needs.

RISK SYSTEM — 3-3 MODEL

Group A (3 players): 85–100% risk, constant damage. Group B (3 players): 70–85% risk, tactical control without losing aggression.

FLOAT SERVE

Always tactical — aimed at zones or specific passers. Aggressive, with unstable trajectory and reading of the rival system.

JUMP-SPIN SERVE

Full: total commitment and confidence, deep to court center. Controlled: in, aimed at a scouted zone.

ERROR & RISK MANAGEMENT

Max 4 errors per set (does not license raising risk above profile). No two missed serves in a row. Individual risk is set before each match — master more than one serve from any spot.

07
Concept & system

Reception

GENERAL PRINCIPLES

Neutralize the rival serve and deliver a high, stable, centered ball so the setter keeps two real options. The system depends on our passers' profile and the rival serve. Push the lines up and shrink the court on floats to pass from above.

VS JUMP-SPIN SERVE

Firm platform, body aligned behind the ball, no hip rotation or loose arms. 3-passer system with constant zone communication. Setter and middle alert to the short serve and net deflections. Goal: height + control, always to ZONE 3.

VS FLOAT SERVE

Two main passers with high responsibility. We shrink the front pin's zone to free him to attack. Ready to pass sideways, opening hips and lifting the platform. Overhand passing enabled.

FLEXIBILITY & ADAPTABILITY

Systems are dynamic tools: they shift by rotation, momentum, performance or serve type. We use whatever combination works best for the team at that moment.

08
Play free

Error Management

  • The error is information. It never stops aggression. Always have a reason why.

TECHNICAL ERROR → movement execution

TACTICAL ERROR → decision in context

  • A hard, deep hit is a good error; a block-out on a high ball from closing the swing is a bad one — technical and tactical.
TEAM KEY   Play aggressive, with intent and no fear of failing.

CRITICAL MOMENTS

  • Under pressure, we simplify.
  • Brief communication, no noise.
  • Ball security — from the freeball, always through Zone 3, up to set quality.
  • Highest-probability attack.
  • Clear roles — we listen to the staff and execute.

From staff to court

Game Plan

PREPARATION

STAFF
  • Rival analysis: tendencies, rotations, objectives, rival serve types.
  • Game-plan build: offensive and defensive priorities.
  • Team delivery: material for prior study.

EXECUTION

THE WEEK
  • Video — Thursday: confirm patterns, clear doubts.
  • Training: apply situations, decisions and adjustments.
  • Match-day review: roles, tactical focus, priorities.

RESPONSIBILITY

PLAYERS
  • Know the plan and your role.
  • Trust the staff's analysis.
  • Adapt fast to in-match tweaks.
  • Hold tactical coherence under pressure.
  • Exploit rival weaknesses — leverage our strengths, don't adapt to theirs.

10
Measure to improve

KPIs & Metrics

DAILY MOTIVATION · PROFESSIONALISM · CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

Team KPIs

  • % Serve
  • % Reception
  • % Block (# and +)
  • % Block (#)
  • Middle attack
  • High-ball attack
  • Quick-ball attack
  • Attack off pass # / +
  • Attack off pass !
  • Attack off pass –
  • Transition attack

Reference: last tournament data → the baseline to beat every day.

How it works

  • Daily team targets (e.g. 28% pass A, 15% high ball, 10% block #). Miss 2–3 → day not met; hit most → day won.
  • Live feedback: an assistant scouts the session; values updated on the board at every pause.
  • Individual reports: each player has their sheet in Drive with daily stats.
  • Monthly report: individual & team KPIs, direction charts, comparisons and evolution.

Culture

  • Reward: targets met → a mini-set as a treat. Internal competition with a running table.
  • Consequence: not met → set forfeits. A clear mark that today wasn't at the expected level.
  • Purpose: train at 100% like we play, a clear daily goal, professionalism, healthy competition, instant feedback, continuous improvement.

10
Why we work with data

KPIs & Metrics

Why data?

Professionalism · Clarity · Continuous improvement

Transparency & Professionalism

Data removes perception and bias. Everyone knows exactly what's expected and how it's measured. Performance stops being a 'feeling' and becomes real information. Training gets more serious, clearer and more competitive.

Motivation & Daily Objectives

We train with a concrete purpose. Each day has clear goals → we know if we trained well. Feedback is immediate: pause → numbers → correction.

Continuous Improvement & Accountability

Each player has individual tracking and a monthly evolution report. Data justifies decisions: playing time, roles, adjustments. It fuels healthy internal competition. The team grows because everyone knows what to improve and how.

High-Performance Culture

Data isn't control — it's a tool to grow. It orders us. It motivates us. It makes us accountable. It makes us professionals. It lets us compete at the highest level.
